chapter.title: Wanted: Steve Mercer (Two of Him)
chapter.goal: Steve wants to hide, and to find his mother’s notebook before the crew does.

c5_shack.objective: Open your parents’ boxes. Follow their investigation.
notes: Nora’s copy has been missing since the stakeout on Tuesday the 30th, which is why the crew can charge Steve with kidnapping. Luis says so here.
New sound assets for log: effect.hum_first_reel (one steady low hum under radio static) and effect.hum_last_reel (the same note held by many voices, beating slightly against each other).
Gull, Marsh and Cedar are the club operators Frank calls on in Chapter 10. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point. Use these names in c10_station.
Helen’s note is voiced in her own voice as a memory, as Steve reads it.
context: steve|By sunrise my face was on every wanted poster in the county. I came down out of the trees to Dad’s radio shack, on the bluff above the bay.
steve|Their boxes were still stacked where I’d left them. I’d never been able to open them.
intro: steve|Luis. They’re saying I took Nora.
luis|Nora has been gone since Tuesday night. Carmen hasn’t slept. And I have known you since you were nine years old.
luis|I heard stories about the bay singing when I was a boy. I first heard it myself three years ago. Your father was the only one who asked what it sounded like.

notes.title: Kitchen-table notes
notes.goal: Work out where Mom hid her notebook.
notes.background: Rook asked about Helen’s notebook again and again. In the boxes are forty-five years of notes Helen and Frank left each other on the kitchen table every morning, and one slip addressed to Steve.
lead: steve|Forty-five years of kitchen-table notes. Every morning, one of them left the other one a note.
c5_shack.notes.02
steve|Coltrane was Dad’s favorite record. And weather carts are the little weather tapes we played on air at KBWR.
notes.prompt: Helen’s slip says the notebook is “with the good stuff”. What did that mean in this family?
notes.instruction: Find the slip Frank was answering, then the place where those things are kept. March 2, Helen: “Put the anniversary tape with the good stuff.” March 3, Frank: “Done. It’s on the shelf between the Coltrane and the weather carts, next to the boy’s first night at the desk.” March 9, Helen: “Frank, there is soup in the refrigerator. The other container is paint.” Undated, Helen: “Steven. Notebook is with the good stuff. Your first night at the desk.”

rows.label: Frank’s “Done” answers
rows.feedback: Dad dated his answer March 3. Which earlier note actually asked him to put a tape away?

rows.label: “The good stuff” is
rows.feedback: Where would Dad shelve a Coltrane record beside a weather cart and a tape of my first shift?

hints: Frank says “Done”. Which slip asked him to do something?
Coltrane records and weather carts sit together in one building in town.
Frank’s March 3 note answers a request to put a tape somewhere. Coltrane and weather carts live where Steve used to work.
lines: steve|The good stuff. Dad’s name for the station library.
notes.finding: steve|Dad’s “Done” answers Mom’s March 2 slip: he filed their tape between the Coltrane and the weather carts. The good stuff is the KBWR record library. Mom hid her notebook at my old station.

rig.title: Frank’s receiver
rig.goal: Get Frank’s receiver working and tuned to his radio club.
rig.background: Frank was a ham radio operator, call sign K7BLW. His club still meets on the air every Thursday, on the frequency in his log. The receiver needs a battery pack, and its dial has slipped, so it no longer reads true.
lead: steve|Dad’s receiver. Dead battery, and the dial’s slipped since he last used it.
steve|Every set has a rating card, Dad said. Read it before you plug anything in.
steve|Dad’s rule for packs. Same volts, same center pin, and at least as much current as the card asks for.
steve|His log says the dial reads a little high. The same amount, every time.
rig.prompt: Which battery pack, and where should Steve set the dial to hear the club?
rig.instruction: Pick the pack that matches the receiver card, then set the dial as high as Frank’s log says it reads. Receiver: 12 volts, centre positive, needs 400 mA. RED: 12 volts, centre positive, 300 mA. BLUE: 12 volts, centre positive, 800 mA. GREY: 12 volts, centre negative, 800 mA. Frank’s log: a 3.20 station showed at 3.25 on the dial, and a 3.40 station at 3.45. The club is on 3.56.

descriptions.3.51: A weak carrier slides under the static. The dial correction has gone the wrong way.
descriptions.3.56: The club is close, but every voice is still off-centre. Frank’s log says the dial reads high.
descriptions.3.61: Gull’s call sign resolves through the static. Frank’s Thursday club is live.

receiver.target_description: Gull’s call sign resolves through the static. Frank’s Thursday club is live.

rows.label: Battery pack
feedback: RED cannot supply the required current.
BLUE matches voltage, polarity and current.

rows.label: Set the dial to
feedback: That ignores the drift in Frank’s log.
The dial reads 0.05 high, so the club resolves at 3.61.

hints: Check the centre pin and the current, not the colour.
One pack gives too little current. One has the centre pin the wrong way round.
The dial reads high by the same amount at both of Frank’s stations. Add that amount to 3.56.
lines: c5_shack.rig.01
rig.finding: steve|The BLUE pack has the right polarity and enough current. The dial reads 0.05 high, so the club’s 3.56 sits at 3.61. Dad’s radio is alive.

club.title: Thursday club
club.background: For thirty years Frank signed on to his club the same way: “This is K7BLW, Bellwether.” Nobody has heard that call sign in eighteen months. The club meets on Thursdays, but its old hands keep a set on the frequency every night.
options: Sign on the way Dad did
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Sign on the way Dad did.

lines.direction: his voice catching on his father’s call sign

lines: c5_shack.club.01

lines.text: It’s Steve. Frank’s son. I need your help.

lines.new: operator|This is Gull. It isn’t Thursday, but none of us ever really switch off. Marsh and Cedar are on too. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point these days.

club.finding: steve|Dad’s club answered his call sign: Gull, Marsh and Cedar. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point. They meet every Thursday, and they’ll help.

log.title: The last reel
log.goal: Hear what Frank heard on his last reel.
log.background: Frank’s logbooks show that he and Helen tracked the hum for months. He taped it under his radio static every ninth night. His notes get shorter as the reels get stranger.
lead: steve|Dad’s logbooks. Months of them. Every ninth night, the same hum under his static.
steve|And Mom’s handwriting in the margins. Dates, and the word Meridian, underlined twice.
luis|Your father asked me what the bay sounded like. I told him, like a whole church humming one hymn.
log.prompt: Play Frank’s first ninth-night reel and his last. What changed?
options: The last reel is a copy of the first

wrong.0: Listen past the volume. The last reel isn’t one sound.
wrong.2: They don’t line up at all. The last reel has voices the first one doesn’t.

evidence_labels: Frank’s last reel · the day before the boat
hints: Listen to the texture, not the loudness.
The first reel is one steady sound. The last one beats against itself.
On the last reel the note wobbles against itself, the way several singers do when they hold one pitch.

lines.text: Dad heard voices in the hum, and he wanted my ears on it. Was that the only reason they asked me along?

log.finding: steve|Dad’s last reel isn’t one hum. It’s many voices holding one note. “It isn’t one voice. It’s a choir.” Mom and Dad weren’t out on the bay for the view. They were investigating, and they wanted my ears.

recap: steve|Mom and Dad tracked the hum for months. Dad heard a choir in it. Mom wrote Meridian in the margins.
steve|Dad’s club is back on the air. And Mom’s notebook is in the KBWR record library, at the station that fired me.
steve|Twice today someone stood on the path below the shack. Both times, by the time I looked, he was gone.

outro.text: The good stuff. Dad’s name for the station library. And Mom wrote my first night at the desk, not my first show.

outro: steve|And the KBWR tower is blinking. Five flashes, then dark. Last night it was six.
steve|Six days, Rook said. It’s counting down to the signing.

lines: steve|How is Carmen holding up, Luis?
luis|She cooks. When she is frightened, she cooks for forty people. The freezer is full of tamales.
luis|Take some with you when you go. She would want you fed, even now.
steve|Did Dad ever bring you up here?
luis|Every spring. He tuned that radio for hours, and I fell asleep in that chair.
luis|He said I snored in perfect pitch. It was the nicest thing he ever said to me.
steve|Luis, did Nora seem different to you lately?
luis|Last month she let her mother win an argument about salt. Nora never lets anybody win anything.
luis|I thought she was finally growing up. Now I don’t know what I thought.
steve|What did Dad talk about on Thursday nights?

lines.new: operator|Antennas, mostly. And your mother’s soup. He described every spoonful over the air.
operator|Cedar always said Frank’s soup reports were the best show on the band.
operator|Marsh has the tallest antenna in the county, out past Sentinel Point. Says the fog up there hums at night.

lines: steve|Tell Marsh I’d like to hear that sometime.

lines.new: operator|Marsh will talk your ear off, kid. Bring a thermos.

c5_station.objective: Get into the record library and find Mom’s notebook.
changes: U-timeline (Halcyon bought KBWR a year ago; Steve was let go five weeks ago)
notes: Stephen’s lines before he names himself show the speaker as “Steve Mercer?” (line-level display).
halcyon replaces the dated-stamps quiz with the early-night pattern: Halcyon sent Steve home on ninth nights so the tower could transmit unattended.
The steve narration between out.02 and out.03 carries the plot’s heart beat: Steve watching his own face learn his grief.
Small talk is with the radio host only. Stephen is hidden until the last lead, and a scene ends as soon as its last lead is solved, so a Stephen topic could never be heard.
context: steve|KBWR, after midnight. No humans work here now. Just racks of machines, playing music to nobody.
steve|And my voice, on the station ident, still playing between the songs.

intro.text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our control room!

intro: steve|Two fellas. Somebody else is breathing in here.

automation.title: Unattended console
automation.goal: Get through the maintenance door into the record library.
automation.background: Steve built KBWR’s automation schedule before Halcyon replaced him with it. The maintenance door to the record library unlatches only while the station ident plays: twelve seconds, in Steve’s own voice.
lead: steve|AutoRick’s console. I wrote half these carts myself.
steve|The maintenance door only unlatches while my ident plays. Twelve seconds. But the walk over there takes fifteen.
steve|And the news cart is locked. It only plays on the hour, and it’s twenty past.
automation.prompt: What should Steve queue, and where should he wait?
automation.instruction: Queue two carts so Steve is already at the maintenance door when the ident starts. WEATHER lasts 40 seconds, IDENT 12 seconds and NEWS 1 minute 30. NEWS only plays on the hour. The walk from the console to the door takes 15 seconds.

rows.label: Play first
rows.feedback: I need fifteen seconds to walk there. The ident lasts twelve, and the news cart won't play off the hour.

rows.label: Play second
rows.feedback: The door listens for the station ident. I want it to hear that after I've crossed the room.

rows.label: Wait at
rows.feedback: Automation can run the console without me. Where do I need to be when the ident starts?

hints: Can Steve cross the room before the ident ends?
Something long has to play while he walks, and it can’t be the locked cart.
The ident lasts twelve seconds and the walk takes fifteen. Play something long enough to walk through, with the ident straight after it.

lines.text: I built this schedule before they replaced me with it. And the door still opens for my voice.

automation.finding: steve|WEATHER gave me forty seconds to cross the room. Then my own voice, on the ident, unlatched the maintenance door.

sleeve.title: First night at the desk
sleeve.goal: Find the sleeve where Helen hid her notebook.
sleeve.background: Helen’s slip said the notebook was “with the good stuff. Your first night at the desk.” KBWR files every master under its original broadcast, never under a repeat.
lead: steve|The record library. Every master we ever made, filed the way Dad taught me.
steve|Mom never wrote my first show. She wrote my first night at the desk. The engineer sits at the desk.

board.instruction: Follow Mom’s words through the duty book to the right sleeve.
evidence: On Tuesday the 4th, Steve sat at the engineer’s desk for the midnight show, and Jo presented.
On Tuesday the 11th, Steve presented at the microphone, and Jo sat at the desk.
On the 18th, Pat played a repeat of the show from the 4th.
KBWR files every master with its original broadcast, never with a repeat.
The blue sleeve holds the original show from the 4th, and the yellow sleeve holds the repeat.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: Which was Steve’s first night at the desk?
Where is that night’s master filed?

board.wrong_text: Steve pulls the wrong sleeve. Mom was always more precise than that.

hints: Mom wrote “at the desk”, not “at the microphone”.
Which Tuesday did Steve sit at the desk? Repeats are never filed as masters.
Find the desk night in the duty book, then the sleeve that holds that night’s original.

lines.new: steve|I knocked the whole shelf over. The blue one landed in my lap.

lines: c5_station.sleeve.01
sleeve.finding: steve|My first night at the desk was the 4th, when I engineered and Jo presented. The original is in the blue sleeve, and Mom’s notebook was in its back pocket. I can’t read a word of it.

halcyon.title: Halcyon’s paperwork
halcyon.goal: Find out why Halcyon really let Steve go.
halcyon.background: The office is full of paperwork from Halcyon Media Holdings, the company that bought KBWR a year ago and replaced Steve with AutoRick five weeks ago. Steve always thought it was about money.
lead: steve|Halcyon Media Holdings. The company that fired me. Their filing is very tidy.
steve|Three early nights in September. Halcyon said they were saving on my overtime.
steve|And the tower log says the tower ran by itself on those same three nights.
halcyon.prompt: What do the duty sheets and the tower log say, side by side?
halcyon.instruction: Compare the dates. Halcyon sent Steve home at 23:30 on September 6, 15 and 24. The tower ran alone from 23:45 on those same nights. Steve’s last shift was September 28. Since then, the tower ran alone on October 3, 12, 21 and 30.

rows.label: Steve’s early nights were
rows.feedback: September 6 to 15 is the same gap as 15 to 24. It wasn't a weekly shift change.

rows.label: The tower transmits alone
rows.feedback: They sent me home at 23:30. The log starts the unattended run at 23:45. Which happened first?
options: Only once the building is empty

rows.label: Next unattended night
rows.feedback: Start at the last October entry and carry the same gap into November.

hints: Count the days from September 6 to September 15.
The tower only ran alone after Steve had gone home, never while he was at work.
The gap between the dates is the same every time. Count it once more from October 30.
lines: c5_station.halcyon.01
halcyon.finding: steve|Halcyon sent me home early every ninth night, and the tower transmitted alone as soon as I left. Then they let me go for good. The next unattended night is November 8.

stephen.title: The man with my face
stephen.goal: Find out how far the other man’s memory reaches, without feeding him the answers.
stephen.background: The man with Steve’s face remembers breakfast with Mom and Dad. He seems to know nothing about the wanted posters. Steve lays three things on the table and lets him talk first, the way June would.
lead: steve|...The man Carmen saw at the market. My face.

lead.new: stephen|It’s a good face. You’re not doing it any favors.
stephen|The last thing I remember of home is breakfast in Dad’s shack. Mom’s jam jar, with the chip in the blue lid.
stephen|A tape that says Mom, last call? Mom never leaves voicemails. She calls back.

lead: steve|Then turn this poster over, and read it.

board.instruction: Sort each thing by when he could have learned it.
evidence: Before he sees anything, he describes breakfast in Dad’s shack: Mom’s jam jar, with a chip in the blue lid.
He looks at the cassette labelled MOM, LAST CALL, and shrugs. “Mom never leaves voicemails. She calls back.”
The wanted poster lies face down. He can read it only after Steve turns it over.
Mom’s last call came from the boat, the night after that breakfast.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: What does he remember on his own?
What did he only learn tonight?

board.wrong_text: That isn’t what he said. Listen again before deciding what he knows.

hints: Which detail did he give before Steve showed him anything?
He shrugged at the tape. He read the poster only after Steve turned it over.
Sort by when he could know it: before he walked in, not at all, or after Steve showed him tonight.

lines.new: stephen|The tank slate said sixty-one was the memory index, not sixty-one percent of a person. Last stable binding: breakfast in Dad’s shack.

lines: stephen|Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.
c5_station.stephen.02
stephen.finding: steve|He remembers Mom’s chipped jam jar, and nothing of home after that breakfast. He doesn’t know about the boat. He doesn’t know they’re gone.

recap: steve|Mom’s notebook was in the blue sleeve, in a shorthand I can’t read. Halcyon cleared the building every ninth night so the tower could talk to the ship.
steve|And the man with my face had a sixty-one-percent memory index, but his last stable binding ended at breakfast before the boat. Eighteen months of my life were missing.

outro.text: No. I had breakfast with them. It never got as far as the boat.

outro.new: steve|I watched my own face learn it. Eighteen months, all at once.

outro: steve|You woke up on the ship.
stephen|In a glass tank, last Friday. Cold, wet, with the index at sixty-one. A very tall man gave me a crew pass, an earpiece and a job.
stephen|Find the man with my face. Find Mom’s notebook. Report in every single night.
steve|Carmen saw you at the market.
stephen|She hugged me and said I looked well. I didn’t know why that made me want to cry. After that I watched June’s house all week. Today I followed you up the path to Dad’s shack. Twice.
stephen|Then I heard you through the shack window. The good stuff, the station library. So I came here first, and waited for you in the dark.

outro.new: steve|Then the earpiece in his hand clicked. I knew that voice. It was the one on the ship’s intercom, the one that opened my chair.
saren|Hunter. You missed your report. Where is the original?
outro.direction: small and clear, from the earpiece in Stephen’s hand

outro.new: steve|Stephen looked at me for a long time. Then he lifted the earpiece to his ear.
stephen|Not at the station. He’s gone north, toward the border. I’m following him.

outro: stephen|There. I’ve just lied to a spaceship for you. I think that makes us brothers.
steve|Then tell me one thing, brother. Why didn’t they send copies of Mom and Dad home, the way they sent Nora’s?
stephen|The tall man said Mom’s scan was damaged. A copy of her wouldn’t know where the notebook is. And the town had already buried them. The empty boat came back.
stephen|So they keep them asleep. As long as Mom sleeps, the notebook has an owner they can ask.

lines: steve|All right, machine. What’s the weather tonight?

lines.new: autorick|Sunny and seventy-two, folks! Perfect beach weather out there in Bellwether!

lines: steve|It’s midnight in November. That was yesterday’s weather, and it was wrong then too.
steve|Can I make a request? Anything with a saxophone.

lines.new: autorick|Our request line is closed! Every song is chosen with love by Halcyon Media Holdings.

lines: steve|Chosen with love. By a spreadsheet in another state.

lines.new: autorick|Good night, Bellwether! Keep one ear on the water!

lines: steve|I wrote that sign-off. My first week on the night desk.
steve|Dad called the station the next morning just to say he heard it.
